bib.title: The Curious Case of Neural Text Degeneration

question: What decoding strategy yields open-ended text from a language model that is both high quality and as diverse as human text?
hypothesis: Likelihood maximization is inappropriate for open-ended generation, and pure sampling fails because of an unreliable low-probability tail that truncating to a dynamic nucleus removes.
contributions: Show maximization-based decoding degenerates and pure sampling is incoherent
Compare decoders against human text on perplexity, Zipf, Self-BLEU, repetition and HUSE

method.summary: Generate 5,000 continuations with GPT-2 Large under many decoding methods and compare likelihood, vocabulary, diversity, repetition and HUSE against human WebText.

datasets.name: WebText held-out portion
datasets.preprocessing: conditioning on initial paragraph restricted to 1-40 tokens

other.note: Fig 1 caption calls Large and XL 774M and 1542M; text says 762M

inference.decoding: greedy; beam (b=16, also 32 in Fig 1); stochastic beam b=16; pure sampling; temperature; top-k; nucleus
inference.temperature: t=0.9 sampling; t=0.7 with top-k=40; sweeps t 0.1-1.0
inference.samples: 5,000 passages per method; Self-BLEU uses 1000 generations vs 4999 references; HUSE 200 generations x 20 annotators
inference.prompting: condition on first paragraph (1-40 tokens) of held-out WebText docs

metrics.name: Perplexity
metrics.definition: perplexity of generated text under the generating model; closer to gold is better

metrics.name: Self-BLEU4
metrics.definition: BLEU of each generation using all other generations as references; lower means more diverse

metrics.name: Zipf coefficient
metrics.definition: Zipfian exponent s of rank-frequency distribution; compared to human

metrics.name: Repetition %
metrics.definition: share of generations where a phrase (min length 2) repeats at least three times at the end of the first 200 tokens

metrics.name: HUSE
metrics.definition: KNN discriminator (k=13) over LM probability and human typicality judgements

eval.protocol: single run per setting; no seeds or significance tests stated; closeness to human value is the criterion except HUSE

availability.data: all generations at same GitHub; WebText at openai/gpt-2-output-dataset

results.claim: Beam search (size 32) degenerates into repetition; at b>=64 GPT-2 Large and XL stop immediately
Probability of a repeated phrase increases with each repetition (positive feedback loop)
Human text per-token probability is much lower than beam search text; natural language does not maximize probability
Self-BLEU: t in [0.5,1] and k in [1,100] give high self-similarity; p in [0.9,1) closely matches human

limits: Only GPT-2 Large (762M) and English web text; no instruction-tuned models
Single run, no seeds or confidence intervals stated
HUSE for top-k and nucleus is computed on a distribution interpolated with mass 0.1, a proxy
Authors say future work should combine training-time and inference-time fixes and a semantic utility
Beam search repetition falls with beam width mainly because generations get shorter (Appendix A)
